lesson.title: Saturday Point #1
lesson.hook: One point on your serve, built from this week's lessons. Two choices each shot: the one you want to hit, and the one that wins.
lesson.memHTML: Serve to open it. Earn the finish.
lesson.tomorrow: In your next match, play this pattern once on purpose: serve wide, hit into the open court, then look behind them.

steps.name: They guard the middle
steps.sit: 30-30, deuce court. The returner stands close to the middle to protect their backhand.
opts: Down the T, for the ace
Wide, to pull them off the court
steps.payoff: Wide drags them off the court. They can only block it back.
steps.principle: The serve asks the question. Ask one that opens the court.
steps.why: Standing in the middle, they cover the T easily. Wide makes them reach outside the sideline, so the return is a block and the court behind it is open.
steps.take: Returner in the middle? Serve wide.

lines.A: Short, but they're still in the middle. Nothing is open.
lines.B: Right: off the court. They block it short, and the court is open.

steps.name: Pulled wide
steps.sit: Your wide serve has them reaching outside the sideline.
steps.payoff: Stretched that far, all they can do is block it short.
steps.principle: Where you serve decides what they can send back.
steps.why: At full stretch they can't swing. A blocked return through the middle is all that's left, so you can start moving in before they hit it.
steps.take: Pulled them wide? Expect the short block and move in.

lines.A: Right: a block, short through the middle. You're moving in early.
lines.B: Not from out there. Stretched, they can only block it short.

steps.name: The short ball
steps.sit: Their blocked return sits up short. They're still out wide, scrambling back.
steps.payoff: Their position earned the attack. The open court makes them sprint.
steps.principle: Short is an invitation. Their position decides if you accept.
steps.why: They're stranded wide, so the open court is the attack their position gave you. The drop gives them a short run straight at the ball.
steps.take: They're stranded wide? Hit the +1 into the open court.

lines.A: They run it down and punish it. You're stretched.
lines.B: Right: they sprint, and only just reach it. You're set early.

steps.name: At full sprint
steps.sit: They reach your +1 at a full sprint.
opts: A high float, to buy time
A hard pass down the line
steps.payoff: A player at full stretch buys time with height. Get ready for the float.
steps.principle: Height and depth buy back the time a stretch took.
steps.why: At a full sprint they can't hit through the ball. The only safe answer is a high float, the same one you learned in The Short Ball, from their side.
steps.take: They're sprinting? Expect the float and get set.

lines.A: Right: a high float. You're set early with time to choose.
lines.B: Not at a full sprint. All they can do is float it.

steps.name: Their float
steps.sit: Their float sits up. You're set. They're still racing back toward the middle.
steps.payoff: The ball, your balance and the space all said yes. Behind them, they can't turn.
steps.principle: Risk is right when the ball, your balance and the space all support it.
steps.why: A high ball, a set player and an opponent running the other way earn the line. The safe middle ball runs straight into them and hands the point back.
steps.take: Set, and they're running back? Go behind them.

lines.A: It runs straight into them. Back to even; you're only just in time.
lines.B: Right: behind them, and they can't turn. Winner.
